doctrineRequirements: opponent build capabilities are unknown until revealed by observable combat actions; future sensor scans may populate the same knowledge state
established combat prefers Active Sensor but may fall back to Passive rather than starve a useful main-weapon package
ECCM activates only against observed ECM when it materially restores Firm track
useful main-weapon operation is a core Tactical Power package; finite-ammo weapons and PDS are not powered after ammunition exhaustion
unknown capability may justify residual defensive readiness but cannot displace the core combat package
PDS activates from residual power for unresolved readiness or imminent missile threat and is suppressed after a known non-Missile capability
Shield Hardener activates from residual power while threat is unresolved or Energy is known and is suppressed after known non-Energy capability

single-main Kinetic/Energy preserves a legal ship attack; Held Main covers otherwise-unserved imminent missile capacity only when no legal ship-fire opportunity exists, while dual-main ships may hold one bank to supplement excess threat
dual-main Kinetic/Energy may hold one bank to supplement funded PDS when imminent PDS-visible subflights exceed Reaction Capacity
PDS telemetry distinguishes magazine Flights from PDS-visible subflights
interpretationBoundary: CP146 changes doctrine/AI logic and observation terminology only. It promotes no weapon, Reactor, PDS, Sensor, EW, defense, AUX, or resource numerical values. CP144/CP145 balance outcomes remain historical evidence under the legacy doctrine and must not be mixed numerically with CP146 outcomes as if the doctrine were unchanged.
nextStage: if native CP146 validates behavior and legacy reproducibility, rerun the broad whole-combat response surface under the accepted contextual doctrine before numerical tuning or Stage B
